questions.question: A particle moves in a straight line with constant acceleration 1.5 m s^-2. While its speed increases from 4 m s^-1 to 10 m s^-1, the distance travelled is: A 24 m, B 28 m, C 40 m, D 56 m.
steps: v = u + at gives t = (10 - 4)/1.5 = 4 s.
A is (change in speed) x t = 6 x 4, which ignores that the speed varies; C is 10 x 4, using the final speed for the whole time.
D is 14 x 4, which leaves out the factor 1/2 in s = (u + v)t/2.

questions.question: A stone is dropped from rest from the top of a vertical cliff and hits the sea 3.0 s later. Modelling the stone as a particle falling freely under gravity, the height of the cliff is: A 14.7 m, B 29.4 m, C 44.1 m, D 88.2 m.
steps: Take downwards as positive: u = 0, a = 9.8 m s^-2, t = 3.0 s.
A is 4.9 x 3 (t not squared); B is 9.8 x 3, which is the final speed, not a height.
D is 9.8 x 3^2, which leaves out the factor 1/2.

questions.question: A cyclist passes a point A with speed 5 m s^-1 and travels along a straight horizontal road with constant acceleration 0.4 m s^-2. She passes the point B 15 s after passing A. Calculate the distance AB.
steps: The acceleration is constant, so use s = ut + (1/2)at^2 with u = 5, a = 0.4 and t = 15.

questions.question: A particle P moves in a straight line with constant acceleration. At time t = 0, P has speed 3 m s^-1. During the fifth second of its motion, from t = 4 s to t = 5 s, P travels 21 m. Find the acceleration of P.
steps: Let the acceleration be a m s^-2. The distance in the fifth second is s(5) - s(4), where s(t) = 3t + (1/2)at^2.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with speed 11 m s^-1 from a point 2 m above horizontal ground. The ball is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity. Show that the ball hits the ground 2.41 s after it is thrown, to 3 significant figures.
steps: Take upwards as positive: u = 11, a = -9.8 and the ground is at displacement s = -2.
t = (11 + sqrt(121 + 39.2))/9.8 = (11 + sqrt(160.2))/9.8, rejecting the negative root.
t = 2.41 s (3 s.f.), as required.

questions.question: Car P starts from rest at a point A and moves along a straight horizontal road with constant acceleration 1.5 m s^-2. At the instant P leaves A, car Q passes A travelling at a constant speed of 18 m s^-1 in the same direction as P. The cars are modelled as particles and t is the time in seconds after P leaves A. Write down expressions, in terms of t, for the distance of P from A and the distance of Q from A at time t.
steps: Q: constant speed 18 m s^-1, so s = 18t.

questions.question: Car P starts from rest at A with constant acceleration 1.5 m s^-2. At the same instant car Q passes A with constant speed 18 m s^-1 in the same direction. Show that P overtakes Q 24 s after leaving A.
steps: P overtakes Q when both are the same distance from A: 0.75t^2 = 18t.
So P overtakes Q 24 s after leaving A (shown).

questions.question: Car P starts from rest at A with constant acceleration 1.5 m s^-2 and overtakes car Q 24 s later. Find the speed of P at the instant it overtakes Q.
steps: Use v = u + at with u = 0, a = 1.5 and t = 24.

questions.question: Car P starts from rest at A with constant acceleration 1.5 m s^-2. At the same instant car Q passes A with constant speed 18 m s^-1 in the same direction. P overtakes Q 24 s later. Find the greatest distance between P and Q before P overtakes Q.
steps: The distance of Q ahead of P at time t is d = 18t - 0.75t^2 for 0 <= t <= 24.
d is greatest when the cars have the same speed: 1.5t = 18, so t = 12 s (the same result comes from setting dd/dt = 18 - 1.5t = 0).
Greatest distance = 108 m.

questions.question: Car P is modelled as accelerating at a constant 1.5 m s^-2 from rest and is found to overtake car Q after 24 s. State one reason why constant acceleration is unrealistic for a real car, and say how the time taken to overtake Q would be affected.
questions.answer: The acceleration of a real car would decrease as its speed rises (resistance grows), so P would take longer than 24 s to overtake Q.
steps: A real car cannot keep a constant acceleration: air resistance (and other resistances) increase with speed, so the resultant force and the acceleration decrease.
P would therefore be slower than the model predicts, so the time taken to overtake Q would be greater than 24 s.
accept: The engine power is limited, so the driving force falls as the speed increases.
Gear changes make the driving force, and so the acceleration, vary.
A real car cannot reach its acceleration instantly from rest (the driving force builds up over a short time).

questions.question: The speed-time graph of a particle consists of straight line segments joining the points (0, 0), (5, 12), (11, 12) and (19, 0), where t is in seconds and the speed is in m s^-1. The total distance travelled by the particle is: A 150 m, B 72 m, C 114 m, D 228 m.
steps: Distance = area under the speed-time graph.
The graph is a trapezium with parallel sides 19 s (the whole journey) and 6 s (the constant-speed section) and height 12 m s^-1: area = (19 + 6)/2 x 12 = 150 m.
B is 6 x 12, only the constant-speed section; C is the triangle (1/2) x 19 x 12, which ignores the constant-speed section.
D is 19 x 12, a rectangle that makes no allowance for the speed starting and ending at zero.

questions.question: The velocity-time graph of a particle moving along a straight line is a straight line passing through (0, 6) and (4, -2), where t is in seconds and the velocity is in m s^-1. The particle is instantaneously at rest at time t, and has acceleration a, where: A t = 1.5 s and a = -4 m s^-2, B t = 2 s and a = -2 m s^-2, C t = 3 s and a = +2 m s^-2, D t = 3 s and a = -2 m s^-2.
questions.answer: D: t = 3 s and a = -2 m s^-2
steps: Acceleration = gradient = (-2 - 6)/4 = -2 m s^-2.
The velocity is v = 6 - 2t, which is zero when t = 3 s.

A gets t = 6/4 = 1.5 by dividing by the time 4 instead of the gradient 2, and gets a = (-2 - 6)/2 = -4 by dividing by 2 instead of 4; B takes the midpoint of 0 and 4 as the time, but v = 2 m s^-1 at t = 2.
C has the correct time but the wrong sign for the acceleration: the velocity is decreasing, so the gradient is negative.

questions.question: A car travels along a straight road. Its speed-time graph consists of straight line segments joining the points (0, 0), (8, 20), (20, 20) and (26, 0), where t is in seconds and the speed is in m s^-1. Calculate the average speed of the car over the whole 26 s.
steps: Total distance = area under the graph = (1/2)(8)(20) + (12)(20) + (1/2)(6)(20).
Average speed = total distance / total time = 380/26 = 14.6 m s^-1 (3 s.f.).

questions.question: A particle moves along a straight line through a fixed point O. Its displacement s metres from O at time t seconds is given by a graph made up of three straight line segments joining the points (0, 0), (5, 20), (9, 20) and (15, -10). Describe the motion of the particle in each of the three stages, giving its velocity in each stage and the time at which it passes through O after t = 0.
questions.answer: 0-5 s: away from O at 4 m s^-1; 5-9 s: at rest 20 m from O; 9-15 s: velocity -5 m s^-1, back towards O, passing O at t = 13 s.
steps: 0 to 5 s: the gradient is 20/5 = 4, so the particle moves away from O with velocity 4 m s^-1.
5 to 9 s: the gradient is 0, so the particle is at rest, 20 m from O.
9 to 15 s: the gradient is (-10 - 20)/6 = -5, so the particle moves back towards O with velocity -5 m s^-1 (speed 5 m s^-1).
It passes through O when 20 - 5(t - 9) = 0, so at t = 13 s.
accept: At t = 15 s the particle is 10 m from O on the opposite side from where it started (displacement -10 m).
The particle reverses direction at t = 9 s, moving from rest to motion back through O.

questions.question: A particle moves in a straight line. Its velocity v m s^-1 at time t seconds, for 0 <= t <= 6, is given by a straight-line graph passing through the points (0, -8) and (6, 10). Find the total distance travelled by the particle in the first 6 seconds.
steps: The gradient is 18/6 = 3, so v = 3t - 8, which is zero when t = 8/3 s.
For 0 <= t <= 8/3 the velocity is negative: distance = (1/2)(8/3)(8) = 32/3 m.
For 8/3 <= t <= 6 the velocity is positive: distance = (1/2)(6 - 8/3)(10) = (1/2)(10/3)(10) = 50/3 m.
Total distance = 32/3 + 50/3 = 82/3 = 27.3 m (3 s.f.). The displacement would be 50/3 - 32/3 = 6 m, which is not what is asked.

questions.question: A train moves along a straight horizontal track from station A to station B. The train starts from rest at A and accelerates uniformly for 40 s until it reaches speed V m s^-1. It then travels at constant speed V m s^-1 for 160 s, before decelerating uniformly to rest at B, taking 60 s for the deceleration. By considering the area under the speed-time graph, show that the distance AB is 210V metres.
steps: Distance = area under the speed-time graph, found as three parts.
Acceleration stage: (1/2)(40)V = 20V. Constant speed: 160V. Deceleration stage: (1/2)(60)V = 30V.

questions.question: A train accelerates uniformly from rest at A to speed V m s^-1, travels at constant speed V m s^-1 and then decelerates uniformly to rest at B. The distance AB is 210V metres. Given that AB = 6300 m, find the value of V.

The train accelerates uniformly from rest to 30 m s^-1 in 40 s, and later decelerates uniformly from 30 m s^-1 to rest in 60 s. Find the magnitude of the acceleration during the first 40 s and the magnitude of the deceleration during the last 60 s.
steps: Acceleration = gradient of the speed-time graph = 30/40 = 0.75 m s^-2.
Deceleration = 30/60 = 0.5 m s^-2.

questions.question: The train accelerates uniformly from rest at 0.75 m s^-2 for 40 s to a speed of 30 m s^-1. It then travels at 30 m s^-1 for 160 s, before decelerating uniformly at 0.5 m s^-2 to rest. Find the two times, measured from the moment the train leaves A, at which the speed of the train is 18 m s^-1.
steps: Acceleration stage: 0.75t = 18, so t = 24 s.
The constant-speed stage ends at t = 40 + 160 = 200 s; the deceleration begins from 30 m s^-1.
Deceleration stage: 30 - 0.5(t - 200) = 18, so t - 200 = 24.
t = 224 s, which is before the train stops at t = 260 s, so both times are valid.

questions.question: A particle of mass 0.4 kg is moving in a straight line at 6 m s^-1 when it receives an impulse of magnitude 3.2 N s in the direction opposite to its motion. Immediately after receiving the impulse the particle is moving with: A 2 m s^-1 in its original direction, B 2 m s^-1 in the opposite direction, C 8 m s^-1 in the opposite direction, D 14 m s^-1 in its original direction.
questions.answer: B: 2 m s^-1 in the opposite direction
steps: Take the original direction as positive. Impulse = change in momentum: -3.2 = 0.4v - 0.4 x 6.
0.4v = 2.4 - 3.2 = -0.8, so v = -2 m s^-1: the speed is 2 m s^-1 and the direction is reversed.
A has the right speed but ignores the sign of v; C is the change in velocity, 3.2/0.4 = 8 m s^-1, not the final velocity.
D adds the impulse instead of subtracting it: 6 + 8 = 14.

questions.question: Two particles P and Q collide directly on a smooth horizontal surface. The mass of P is 2m and the mass of Q is m. The impulse exerted by P on Q has magnitude J. Which statement is correct? A The impulse exerted by Q on P has magnitude J and acts in the opposite direction, B The impulse exerted by Q on P has magnitude J/2 and acts in the opposite direction, C The speed of P changes by the same amount as the speed of Q, D The total momentum of P and Q increases by J.
questions.answer: A: the impulse on P has magnitude J in the opposite direction
steps: Newton's third law: the impulse of Q on P is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the impulse of P on Q, so A is correct.
B is wrong because the impulses are equal in magnitude whatever the masses.
C is wrong: the speed of P changes by J/(2m) but the speed of Q changes by J/m.
D is wrong: the two impulses cancel, so the total momentum is conserved.

questions.question: Two railway trucks, of masses 1200 kg and 800 kg, are on a straight horizontal track. The 1200 kg truck is moving at 3.5 m s^-1 when it collides with the stationary 800 kg truck. The trucks couple together on impact. Find the speed of the trucks immediately after the collision.
steps: Conservation of momentum, with the trucks moving together afterwards: 1200 x 3.5 = (1200 + 800)v.

questions.question: Particles A and B have masses 0.5 kg and 0.3 kg. They move towards each other along a straight line on a smooth horizontal table, A with speed 4 m s^-1 and B with speed 2 m s^-1, and collide directly. After the collision B moves with speed 3.5 m s^-1 in the direction in which A was moving before the collision. Find the speed of A after the collision and state its direction of motion.
questions.answer: 0.7 m s^-1, in the same direction as before the collision
steps: Take A's original direction as positive. Before: momentum = 0.5 x 4 + 0.3 x (-2) = 1.4 N s.
After: 0.5v + 0.3 x 3.5 = 0.5v + 1.05, where v is the velocity of A.
Conservation of momentum: 1.4 = 0.5v + 1.05, so v = 0.7.
v is positive, so A still moves in its original direction, with speed 0.7 m s^-1.

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.25 kg hits a smooth vertical wall at right angles with speed 12 m s^-1 and rebounds along the same line with speed 8 m s^-1. The ball is in contact with the wall for 0.02 s. Modelling the force exerted by the wall on the ball as constant, find its magnitude.
steps: Take the direction towards the wall as positive: initial velocity 12 m s^-1, final velocity -8 m s^-1.
Impulse = change in momentum = 0.25(-8 - 12) = -5, so the impulse has magnitude 5 N s.
Impulse = force x time, so F = 5/0.02.

questions.question: Particle P of mass 3m and particle Q of mass 2m move in opposite directions along the same straight line on a smooth horizontal surface. They collide directly. Immediately before the collision P has speed 5u and Q has speed 3u. Immediately after the collision P has speed u and is moving in the same direction as before the collision. Find the speed of Q immediately after the collision and state its direction of motion.
questions.answer: 3u, in the original direction of motion of P (the direction of Q is reversed)
steps: Take P's original direction as positive. Before: momentum = 3m(5u) + 2m(-3u) = 9mu.
After: 3m(u) + 2m(v) = 9mu, where v is the velocity of Q.
2mv = 6mu, so v = 3u.
v is positive, so Q moves with speed 3u in P's original direction: Q has reversed direction.

questions.question: Particle P of mass 3m and particle Q of mass 2m move in opposite directions along the same straight line and collide directly. Before the collision P has speed 5u and Q has speed 3u. After the collision Q has speed 3u and its direction of motion is reversed. Find, in terms of m and u, the magnitude of the impulse exerted by P on Q in the collision.
steps: Impulse on Q = change in momentum of Q.
Take P's original direction as positive: Q goes from -3u to +3u, so impulse = 2m(3u - (-3u)) = 2m x 6u.
Magnitude = 12mu N s.

questions.question: In a collision between particles P and Q, the impulse exerted by P on Q has magnitude 12mu N s. State the magnitude and the direction of the impulse exerted by Q on P, giving a reason for your answer.
questions.answer: 12mu N s, in the direction opposite to the impulse exerted by P on Q (Newton's third law).
steps: The magnitude of the impulse exerted by Q on P is 12mu N s.
It acts in the direction opposite to the impulse exerted by P on Q, because by Newton's third law the impulses on P and Q are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
accept: Total momentum is conserved, so the change in momentum of P is equal and opposite to the change in momentum of Q.
Taking the direction of the impulse on Q as positive, the impulse on Q is +12mu N s and the impulse on P is -12mu N s.

questions.question: Particle P of mass 3m and particle Q of mass 2m move in opposite directions along the same straight line and collide directly. Before the collision P has speed 5u and Q has speed 3u. After the collision Q has speed 3u and its direction of motion is reversed, so that the impulse exerted by P on Q has magnitude 12mu N s. Given that this impulse has magnitude 30 N s and that m = 2.5, find the speed of P before the collision.
steps: 12mu = 30 with m = 2.5 gives 30u = 30, so u = 1 m s^-1.
Speed of P before the collision = 5u = 5 m s^-1.
